facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus was described in 2010 from fossils found in the Lameta Formation of Gujarat, India.
facts.quote: It was described in 2010, based on fossils recovered from the Lameta Formation in the Indian state of Gujarat.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rahiolisaurus date to the Maastrichtian stage, between 70 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: These fossils include elements from at least seven different individuals and are believed to have been from the Maastrichtian stage, sometime between 70 and 66 million years ago

facts.statement: Remains of Rahiolisaurus were collected during expeditions in 1995 and 1997 from a 50-square-metre quarry.
facts.quote: During two expeditions, one in 1995 and the other in 1997, numerous remains of abelisaurids were recovered from a single quarry 50 square metres in area.

facts.statement: The holotype of Rahiolisaurus consists of a partial pelvic association and a femur.
facts.quote: The holotype of Rahiolisaurus is represented by a partial association of pelvic elements and a femur that were found in the field.

facts.statement: The genus name Rahiolisaurus honors the village of Rahioli near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus was named after the village of Rahioli, located near the fossil site where the dinosaurs remains were discovered.

facts.statement: The species name gujaratensis means "from Gujarat" in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name, gujaratensis, means "from Gujarat" in Latin.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus was initially estimated at 8 meters long and 2 metric tons, but later allometric estimates suggest a length of 6.22 to 6.75 meters.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus was initially described as a large-sized abelisaurid and around 8 m long and weighing 2 MT, but the allometry-based estimate for different specimens suggest a shorter body length of 6.22 - 6.75 m.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus had short arms with four fingers, a short skull, modest jaw muscles, and short teeth.
facts.quote: Abelisaurids typically had four fingers, short arms, and, to compensate, a heavily constructed head which was the primary tool for hunting; however, the skull was short, they probably had modest jaw musculature, and the teeth were short.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus likely possessed a bite force of approximately 3500 Newtons, similar to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Abelisaurids likely had a bite force similar to Allosaurus at around 3500 N.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus likely lived in the region of the modern Narmada River Valley.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus likely inhabited what is now the Narmada River Valley.

facts.statement: The Lameta Formation, where Rahiolisaurus fossils were found, is known as a sauropod nesting site with sandy soil.
facts.quote: The formation is known for being a sauropod nesting site, yielding several dinosaur eggs, and sauropod herds likely chose sandy soil for nesting

facts.statement: In 2014, Rahiolisaurus was placed in the subfamily Majungasaurinae, defined by elongated antorbital fenestrae and a widening sagittal crest.
facts.quote: In 2014, the subfamily Majungasaurinae was erected by palaeontologist Thierry Tortosa to separate the newly discovered European Arcovenator, Majungasaurus, Indosaurus, Rahiolisaurus, and Rajasaurus from South American abelisaurids based on physical characteristics such as elongated antorbital fenestrae in front of the eye sockets, and a sagittal crest that widens into a triangular surface towards the front of the head.

facts.statement: Recent 2021 analyses place Rahiolisaurus outside the subfamily Majungasaurinae as a basal brachyrostran.
facts.quote: In 2021, Rahiolisaurus and Dahalokely were again recovered as sister taxa, however they were placed outside of majungasaurinae as basal brachyrostrans.

facts.statement: While theropod eggs have been found in the Lameta Formation, it is unknown if any belong to Rahiolisaurus.
facts.quote: The formation is known for being a sauropod nesting site, yielding several dinosaur eggs, and sauropod herds likely chose sandy soil for nesting; though eggs belonging to large theropods have been found, it is unknown if they belong to Rahiolisaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Deccan Traps volcanism caused a major adverse climate effect on India's dinosaurs or had relatively mild effects.
facts.quote: While some authors have suggested that the Deccan Traps had a major adverse effect on the climate of India and its dinosaur inhabitants, others have suggested that the effects of the volcanism were relatively mild.

facts.statement: Remains of Rahiolisaurus were collected during two expeditions in 1995 and 1997 from a single quarry measuring 50 square meters.
facts.quote: Durante dos expediciones, una en 1995 y la otra en 1997, se recuperaron numerosos restos de abelisáuridos de una sola cantera de 50 metros cuadrados de superficie.

facts.statement: The discovery of seven right tibias of varying sizes suggests the fossil assemblage included at least seven individuals of different ontogenetic stages.
facts.quote: Debido al descubrimiento de siete tibias derechas de diferentes tamaños, se sugirió que el ensamblaje estaba formado por al menos siete individuos de diferentes etapas ontogenéticas.

facts.statement: The holotype of Rahiolisaurus consists of an association of partial pelvic elements and a femur found in the field.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Rahiolisaurus está representado por una asociación parcial de elementos pélvicos y un fémur que se encontraron en el campo.

facts.statement: The genus name Rahiolisaurus is derived from the village of Rahioli, located near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus recibió su nombre del pueblo de Rahioli, ubicado cerca del sitio de fósiles donde se descubrieron los restos de dinosaurios.

facts.statement: In 2014, paleontologist Thierry Tortosa erected the subfamily Majungasaurinae to separate Rahiolisaurus and related genera from South American abelisaurids based on features like elongated preorbital fenestrae and a sagittal crest widening into a triangular surface.
facts.quote: En 2014, la subfamilia Majungasaurinae fue erigida por el paleontólogo Thierry Tortosa para separar a los recién descubiertos Arcovenator, Majungasaurus, Indosaurus, Rahiolisaurus y Rajasaurus de los abelisáuridos sudamericanos basándose en características físicas como las fenestras antorbitales alargadas delante de las cuencas de los ojos y una cresta sagital que se ensancha en una superficie triangular hacia la parte delantera de la cabeza.

facts.statement: It is debated whether abelisaurid migration occurred between Europe and India via Africa or through the Dras-Kohistan volcanic island arc, though these explanations remain questionable.
facts.quote: Es posible que la migración haya ocurrido entre Europa e India a través de África dada su proximidad a ambos, y el arco volcánico de islas Dras-Kohistan puede haber permitido el salto de isla en isla y un camino indirecto hacia Asia, aunque estas son explicaciones todavía cuestionables.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian epoch in an arid to semi-arid landscape with a river, likely providing shrub cover near water, within the Lameta Formation formed between Deccan Traps volcanic episodes.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus se ha encontrado en la Formación Lameta, una unidad de roca fechada radiométricamente en el Maastrichtiense de finales del Cretácico que representa un paisaje árido o semiárido con un río que lo atraviesa, probablemente proporcionando una cubierta de arbustos cerca del agua, que se formó entre episodios de vulcanismo en las Traps del Decán.

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus likely inhabited what is now the Narmada River valley.
facts.quote: Rahiolisaurus probablemente habitó lo que ahora es el valle del río Narmada.

facts.statement: While eggs belonging to large theropods have been found in the Lameta Formation, it is unknown if they belong to Rahiolisaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque se han encontrado huevos pertenecientes a grandes terópodos, se desconoce si pertenecen a Rahiolisaurus.

facts.statement: Dinosaurs in India likely went extinct due to volcanic activity approximately 350,000 years before the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
facts.quote: Los dinosaurios en la India probablemente se extinguieron debido a la actividad volcánica alrededor de 350.000 años antes del Límite Cretácico-Paleógeno.

facts.statement: The genus Rahiolisaurus was named by Novas and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Rahiolisaurus (genus), Novas et al. 2010

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: Rahiolisaurus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
